title: validate_session_urls accepts schemeless URLs
description: validate_session_urls splits on '://' and takes .next(). A URL like '//host/path' (protocol-relative) has no '://', so split yields ['//host/path'] and .next() returns '//host/path', which is neither 'http' nor 'https', causing a false-positive rejection. More critically, a URL like 'javascript:alert(1)' splits on '://' as ['javascript', ...] and passes the check — but the real danger is a URL such as 'https' (bare word with no '://' at all) which yields scheme='https' and passes even though it is not a real URL. The validator should use url::Url::parse to extract the scheme rather than string splitting.
